method: 6 Sonnet judges (11 names each) on the recorded A/B/C scale with the v2.1 stage 2 admissibility vocabulary; one Opus auditor on every A and a quarter of the C verdicts

audit_changes.reason: pre-commercial, EUR5.7m revenue is grants, EUR34m loss, plant unfinanced
audit_changes.summary: Carbios licenses an enzymatic PET depolymerization process but operates no plant; FY2025 operating revenue of EUR5.7m is grants, subsidiary service fees and rebilled financing costs, not product or license sales, against a EUR34.3m net loss and EUR59m cash. Financial close on the Longlaville plant missed the September 30, 2026 target, so the mechanism is a single unproven breakthrough with no sold flow behind it. The A card carried an empty reason and its own summary conceded limited commercial revenue and continuing losses.

audit_changes.reason: two-thirds managed services outsourcing; billing monetization, not connectivity capacity
audit_changes.summary: Amdocs sells BSS/OSS, charging and network orchestration to telecom operators, but managed-services arrangements were a record 66 percent of revenue (about $3.0bn) in fiscal 2025 at a 38 percent gross margin, which is an outsourcing book, not the license/subscription platform the A card claimed. The orchestration and rollout automation piece is a real mechanism on connectivity; the billing and monetization majority is a carrier revenue-extraction layer sold as headcount.

audit_changes.reason: no host flow named, power is captive smelter input
audit_changes.summary: Chalco mines bauxite and produces alumina and primary aluminum in China, generating thermal, wind and solar power largely to feed its own smelters. The recorded reason called it a captive-territory regulated utility, which it is not; it is an extractive metals producer, and the correct v2.1 cut is that no host energy flow is named because the generation is an internal input rather than a product sold.

rows.reason: no host flow named, holding company of unrelated equity stakes
rows.summary: Aker ASA is a Norwegian industrial holding company owning listed and unlisted stakes across oil and gas, offshore vessels, krill nutrition, property, software and renewables. It sells no single energy product itself but manages a portfolio of controlling equity interests in operating subsidiaries.

rows.reason: no host flow named, no energy segment disclosed
rows.summary: AGC Inc. manufactures architectural and automotive glass, electronics materials, chemicals and ceramics for construction, display and semiconductor customers worldwide. Its product lines are glass and chemical materials, not an energy delivery or grid-support mechanism.

rows.reason: no host flow named, no energy segment disclosed
rows.summary: Berli Jucker manufactures and distributes packaging, tissue, snacks, healthcare products and retail supply chain services in Thailand. It is a diversified consumer-goods and distribution conglomerate with no energy-sector mechanism.

rows.reason: food not largest segment, financial services dominates
rows.summary: CITIC Limited is a Chinese conglomerate whose largest business is comprehensive financial services (banking, securities, insurance), alongside manufacturing, materials and urbanization units. Food and consumer products sit as a minor line inside its New Consumption segment, not the core business.

rows.reason: no host flow named, health not a disclosed segment
rows.summary: Ai Holdings sells surveillance cameras, card systems, measuring instruments and office communication equipment to businesses and institutions in Japan. A small line of medical-institution card and ID systems does not make health its business.

rows.reason: no host number, health one vertical among many acquisitions
rows.summary: AIAI Holdings is a recently renamed roll-up vehicle that says it will acquire and integrate companies across construction, healthcare, defense, blockchain and government services using a proprietary AI layer. It has no disclosed operating health business or revenue base yet.

rows.reason: no host flow named, no water segment disclosed
rows.summary: CK Hutchison operates global container ports, retail chains (Watsons, PARKnSHOP), infrastructure and telecom businesses. None of its four disclosed segments involves water supply, treatment or distribution.

rows.reason: no host number, water membranes minor line in materials mix
rows.summary: Asahi Kasei sells specialty materials, semiconductor and battery components, homes, and healthcare products, with water-treatment membranes (Microza) as one small product line inside its large Materials segment. The water mechanism exists but is not separable or disclosed as a standalone segment.

rows.reason: no host flow named, no water segment disclosed
rows.summary: Ayala Corporation is a Philippine conglomerate in real estate, hotels, banking, insurance and telecom. None of its described business lines touches water supply or treatment.

rows.reason: no host flow named, plumbing distribution not water infrastructure
rows.summary: Bidvest Group distributes healthcare products, power tools, electrical cable, bathroom and plumbing fixtures, and freight-handling services across South Africa and internationally. Its Plumblink plumbing-products distribution is commodity retail, not a water-system mechanism.

rows.reason: no host flow named, no water segment disclosed
rows.summary: Aica Kogyo manufactures decorative panels, adhesives, resins and coating materials for construction and industrial customers in Japan and Asia. Its chemical and building-materials products have no connection to water supply or treatment.

rows.reason: diversified conglomerate, water one segment among many
rows.summary: Berjaya is a Malaysian conglomerate selling consumer retail, hotels, gaming, motor vehicles, financial services and property to consumers and businesses across Asia. Its water supply infrastructure and potable water production is one minor line among dozens of unrelated segments.

rows.reason: no host flow named, printer/camera maker not an energy business
rows.summary: Canon designs and sells printers, cameras, medical imaging equipment and industrial lithography tools to consumers, offices and hospitals worldwide. Nothing in its business models or corrects any energy-grid flow.

rows.reason: pre-revenue agtech shell, no host number disclosed
rows.summary: Braiin sells IoT sensors, connectivity and software to help farmers monitor and improve crop and livestock productivity in Australia and New Zealand. It is a tiny recently-listed SPAC subsidiary with no disclosed material revenue to size any food-flow correction.

rows.reason: data-center networking gear, no health host flow named
rows.summary: Arista builds and sells cloud/data-center networking switches and its EOS software to cloud providers, internet firms, financial and government customers. It serves general enterprise data infrastructure with no disclosed healthcare-specific product or segment.

rows.reason: consumer PC/phone maker, no health host flow named
rows.summary: ASUS designs and sells laptops, phones, motherboards, graphics cards, routers and other consumer/enterprise electronics globally. None of its disclosed product lines target a health-specific need.

rows.reason: 3D printing mechanism diluted by industrial segment mix
rows.summary: 3D Systems sells 3D printers, materials and software split between a Healthcare Solutions segment (dental, medical device, bioprinting) and an Industrial Solutions segment (manufacturing, aerospace). Healthcare became the larger segment by Q4 2025, but industrial/unrelated printing revenue still dilutes the health-specific mechanism.

rows.reason: commodity petrochemical maker, recycled PET one line among virgin plastics
rows.summary: Alpek produces and sells PTA, virgin PET resin, polyester fiber, polypropylene and fertilizers to packaging, textile and industrial customers across the Americas. It does offer recycled PET, but that is a minority product line within a much larger virgin-petrochemical commodity business.

rows.reason: commodity packaging/tissue maker, not a circulation service layer
rows.summary: Cascades manufactures and sells fiber-based packaging (food, protective, e-commerce boxes) and tissue paper products to businesses and retailers in Canada and the US, using significant recycled fiber content. It is a commodity manufacturer sized by tonnage, not a scalable service or platform correcting the materials-circulation deficit directly.

rows.reason: pre-commercial, EUR5.7m revenue is grants, EUR34m loss, plant unfinanced
rows.summary: Carbios develops and licenses enzymatic technology that biologically depolymerizes PET plastic and textile waste back into virgin-grade raw materials for recycling, selling the process to industrial partners like Wankai. This is a direct, scalable mechanism for closing the plastics-circulation loop, though the company remains early-stage with limited commercial revenue and reported roughly EUR51.7 million cash and continuing net losses as of FY2025.

rows.reason: no host flow named, power is captive smelter input
rows.summary: Chalco mines bauxite and coal and produces alumina, aluminum and thermal/wind/solar electricity mainly for its own smelting operations and regional grids in China. Its energy segment is captive to internal production needs, not a scalable product sold as an energy-correcting service.

rows.reason: commodity steel producer, recycling/renewables one segment among four
rows.summary: Aperam produces and sells stainless and specialty steel products to aerospace, automotive, construction and energy customers worldwide, with a dedicated Recycling & Renewables segment collecting and processing stainless scrap. The core business remains commodity steel manufacturing, with the recycling/renewables mechanism only one of four segments.

rows.reason: diversified specialty chemicals, no host flow named
rows.summary: Ashland sells specialty additives and ingredients (pharma excipients, personal-care ingredients, nutrition additives, intermediates) to consumer and industrial manufacturers. Its four segments span pharma, personal care and general chemicals, with no dedicated energy-materials business line.

rows.reason: alloy/tube maker for energy plus medical, industrial mix dilutes it
rows.summary: Alleima makes stainless steel tubes, bars and alloys used in oil and gas extraction, petrochemical processing and heat exchangers, alongside medical wires and Kanthal heating elements. The energy-sector tubing is a real mechanism but sits within a broader industrial-materials portfolio.

rows.reason: renewable energy is minor segment, no host number
rows.summary: AlzChem produces specialty chemicals, adhesives, composites and agricultural/metallurgical intermediates from lime, carbon and electricity, selling into chemical, food and defense industries. Renewable-energy applications are only a small piece of its Specialty Chemicals segment, not a disclosed primary line.

rows.reason: energy one of many end markets, no host flow named
rows.summary: 5N Plus makes specialty semiconductor compounds, wafers, ultra-high-purity metals and pharmaceutical ingredients sold across renewable energy, security, space, medical imaging and industrial customers. Solar-cell materials are one product line among several unrelated end markets, with no disclosed energy-specific segment.

rows.reason: pre-revenue fusion concept, not an operating business
rows.summary: American Fusion is developing an early-stage aneutronic fusion energy platform called Texatron aimed at industrial and grid deployment. The company has no commercialized product and appears pre-revenue.

rows.reason: pre-revenue bioplastics tech, no host flow named
rows.summary: Avantium develops bio-based plastics and chemical technologies (FDCA, PEF, catalytic sugar conversion) aimed at packaging and textile applications, not energy materials. The business is largely R&D and licensing stage with minimal commercial revenue.

rows.reason: pre-revenue, runway concerns, not an operating business
rows.summary: Blue Biofuels is developing a cellulose-to-sugar conversion process and licensing technology to make sustainable aviation fuel from ethanol. It is a micro-cap, pre-commercial technology developer with negligible revenue.

rows.reason: paints and coatings maker, business does not support food need
rows.summary: Akzo Nobel manufactures decorative paints and performance coatings for construction, marine, automotive, aerospace and industrial customers worldwide. It has no food-ingredients or food-materials business, so it does not address a food-materials need.

rows.reason: food is minor piece of diversified chemicals mix, no host number
rows.summary: Clariant makes specialty chemicals for personal care, home care, agriculture, catalysts and industrial processes, with food-related additives forming only a small part of its Care Chemicals segment. No food-specific segment or revenue figure is disclosed.

rows.reason: chemical distributor, food one line among many, no host number
rows.summary: Azelis distributes specialty chemicals and food ingredients on behalf of manufacturers across life sciences and industrial chemicals markets. As a distributor spanning personal care, pharma, agriculture and many other verticals, food ingredients are not disclosed as its largest or distinct segment.

rows.reason: packaging spans food and beauty too, health share not isolated
rows.summary: Amcor manufactures flexible and rigid packaging, including pharmaceutical delivery devices, closures and dispensing components, alongside packaging for food, beverage and beauty products. The health-related packaging is a real mechanism but diluted within a much broader consumer-packaging mix.

rows.reason: packaging materials serve many industries, health not primary segment
rows.summary: Billerud makes paperboard, containerboard, and pulp-based packaging materials sold to packaging and paper manufacturers across food, industrial, medical and consumer end markets. It is a diversified commodity packaging materials producer, not a health-specific mechanism.

rows.reason: diversified chemical and glass conglomerate, pharma one segment among many
rows.summary: Central Glass produces glass, automotive materials, electronic materials, fluorine compounds and fertilizers, with pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals as just one of several chemical lines. It sells across many industrial customers rather than functioning as a health-sector mechanism.

rows.reason: commodity UV-filter and zinc oxide ingredient supplier mostly to cosmetics
rows.summary: Advance ZincTek manufactures zinc oxide and aluminum oxide powders and dispersions used mainly as UV-filter ingredients in sunscreen and cosmetic formulations, with some pharmaceutical use. It is a small commodity ingredient supplier distributed through third parties rather than a scaled health-mechanism company.

rows.reason: biochemicals sold across agriculture, batteries, food; construction not largest segment
rows.summary: Borregaard develops lignin-based biopolymers, specialty cellulose, and fine chemicals sold into agrochemicals, batteries, food and flavor, pharmaceutical intermediate, and construction-binder markets. Construction/shelter use is only one minor application among many diversified end markets.

rows.reason: marine paint maker; building coatings a minor segment, not core
rows.summary: Chugoku Marine Paints primarily manufactures and sells coatings for ships, yachts, and shipping containers, with protective coatings for bridges and building materials as a smaller secondary line. Its core business is marine paint, not a shelter-materials mechanism.

rows.reason: captive mine operator, commodity metals producer, no product layer
rows.summary: Central Asia Metals owns and operates copper and zinc/lead/silver mining and extraction sites in Kazakhstan and North Macedonia, selling raw base metal output. It is a captive mining operation with no scalable product or service layer.

rows.reason: commodity copper miner; transport division captive to own mines
rows.summary: Antofagasta mines and sells copper, molybdenum, gold and silver concentrates from its own Chilean operations, with a rail/road transport division that mainly serves its own and other mining customers. It is a captive commodity mining business, not a scalable logistics or materials mechanism.

rows.reason: chemical distribution platform real but water treatment one vertical among many
rows.summary: Brenntag distributes and blends industrial and specialty chemicals worldwide, offering logistics, inventory management, and digital ordering services across nutrition, pharma, coatings, and water treatment customers. It has a genuine distribution mechanism, but water treatment is only one of many diluted end markets it serves.

rows.reason: diversified specialty chemicals maker, no host flow named for water
rows.summary: Arkema manufactures adhesives, high-performance polymers, and coating solutions sold into construction, automotive, textiles, and packaging industries. Its product mix has no identifiable water-treatment host flow or dedicated water-sector segment.

rows.reason: water chemicals one segment among mining explosives and other businesses
rows.summary: AECI supplies mining explosives and blasting services alongside industrial chemicals, water treatment chemicals, and crop protection products across multiple segments. Water treatment chemicals form only a minor part of a diversified industrial chemicals and mining-services portfolio.

rows.reason: water treatment products real but diluted by cement, battery, decarbonization mix
rows.summary: Calix develops mineral-processing and environmental technologies, including wastewater treatment and aquaculture water-conditioning products, alongside low-emission lime/cement and battery materials technology. Its water products are a real but small part of a broader decarbonization technology portfolio.

rows.reason: diversified conglomerate, water chemicals not dominant, no host flow named
rows.summary: Aimia is a holding conglomerate mixing specialty water/textile chemicals, synthetic ropes and netting for fishing/marine, and unrelated outdoor advertising. No single water-treatment product line dominates the mixed segment portfolio.

rows.reason: pre-revenue environmental technology developer, dilution-funded
rows.summary: BioLargo develops PFAS/water treatment, odor control and antimicrobial device platforms but has not commercialized at scale. It is a small-cap R&D company funding operations through equity issuance rather than product sales.

rows.reason: general mobile developer tools, no host flow named for health
rows.summary: Aurora Mobile sells push-notification, messaging, analytics and app-usage intelligence APIs to Chinese app developers and lenders, plus financial risk-scoring tools for credit decisions. Nothing in its business is oriented to a health need.

rows.reason: data center landlord/hosting, diluted by crypto-mining infrastructure leasing
rows.summary: Applied Digital builds and leases energized data-center capacity, hosting crypto miners and providing cloud/GPU compute to AI developers. Revenue is growing fast but much of the model is capital-intensive real-estate-like hosting rather than a scalable software product.

rows.reason: IT reseller/VAR, diluted by commodity hardware and license resale
rows.summary: Atea resells IT hardware, cloud licenses and software subscriptions to Nordic and Baltic businesses and governments, wrapped with managed infrastructure and security services. The managed-services layer is real but a large share of revenue is pass-through hardware and license resale.

rows.reason: two-thirds managed services outsourcing; billing monetization, not connectivity capacity
rows.summary: Amdocs sells billing, CRM, network orchestration and monetization software that telecom and media operators run their businesses on. It is a licensed/subscription enterprise software platform with real gross margins, not a services pass-through.

rows.reason: software/hardware reseller diluted by commodity device and license sales
rows.summary: Bytes Technology resells servers, laptops, cloud and non-cloud software licenses across the UK, wrapped with security, cloud and workspace consulting services. The consulting/security layer is a real product-adjacent service but hardware and license resale is a commodity pass-through.

rows.reason: IT staffing/outsourcing services, unrelated academic education segment
rows.summary: CLPS provides IT consulting and staffing for banking and fintech clients in China plus an unrelated academic education business. It sells billable headcount and project services rather than a scalable software product.

rows.reason: going concern material uncertainty, sub-10M revenue software developer
rows.summary: Cirata sells data migration and orchestration software for moving Hadoop/HDFS data to the cloud, but revenue remains under $10 million and auditors flagged a material going-concern uncertainty. The product layer is real but the business is not yet a proven, sustainable operation.

rows.reason: commodity metal smelter/producer, real recycling mechanism diluted by commodity output
rows.summary: Aurubis processes metal concentrates and recycled scrap into copper cathodes, rods, wire and precious metals, selling into industrial markets worldwide. The recycling/circulation function is genuine but the output is largely a commodity metal product rather than a differentiated service layer.

rows.reason: container/logistics equipment manufacturer diluted by finance and offshore drilling segments
rows.summary: CIMC manufactures shipping containers, trucks/trailers, and energy/logistics equipment used to move freight, plus unrelated offshore drilling platforms and a finance/asset-management segment. The core container and logistics-equipment business is a real freight-flow mechanism but is diluted by unrelated capital-intensive segments.

rows.reason: no host flow named; diversified wire maker not food-specific
rows.summary: Bekaert makes steel wire and cord products for tires, construction, agriculture, and energy applications sold to industrial manufacturers worldwide. Its revenue mix spans rubber reinforcement, wire solutions, and ropes with no food-specific product line.

rows.reason: no host flow named; c-parts distributor across all industries
rows.summary: Bufab is a trading company that sources and distributes fasteners and small mechanical C-parts (screws, bolts, clamps, labels) to manufacturers across many industries. It is a procurement and logistics intermediary, not a food-specific mechanism.

rows.reason: commodity wholesale distributor of building products, not a maker
rows.summary: ADENTRA wholesales architectural building products such as doors, mouldings, hardwood plywood, and decking to home builders, distribution yards, and home centers across the US and Canada. It is a distribution intermediary in the construction supply chain rather than a manufacturer with a differentiated product platform.

rows.reason: broad industrial MRO distributor, not need-specific mechanism
rows.summary: Applied Industrial Technologies distributes bearings, power transmission, fluid power, and automation components plus engineered maintenance solutions to industrial customers across many sectors. It is primarily a distribution and light-integration business rather than a scalable proprietary product mechanism tied to one specific need.

rows.reason: no host flow named; transport is one segment among many
rows.summary: ADF Group designs, fabricates, and installs complex steel structures and connections for office towers, commercial buildings, airports, industrial complexes, and transport infrastructure. Transport infrastructure is one of several end markets it serves, not its largest disclosed segment.

rows.reason: no host flow named; water not a disclosed largest segment
rows.summary: Addtech distributes technical products and engineered solutions across six segments spanning automation, electrification, energy, industry, process, and safety for manufacturing and infrastructure customers. Water-related technology is only a minor piece of a highly diversified industrial distribution portfolio.

rows.reason: freight coordination and LTL network raising loads per mile
rows.summary: ArcBest operates an asset-based less-than-truckload freight network alongside an asset-light brokerage segment that sources ground, air, and ocean transportation capacity for shippers. Its combined network and coordination platform improves freight matching and utilization across the truckload and LTL system.
